newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworkers talks at crucial phase - employer.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworkers talks at crucial phase - employer.

text.p: Negotiations on a bitter contracts dispute between Italian metalworkers and employers are at a crucial stage and, the head of employers' association Federmeccanica said on Thursday.
On his way into a fresh round of talks Michele Figurati described the situation as "terrible, very complicated, difficult".

Labour Minister Tiziano Treu, Federmeccanica and metalworkers and engineering unions were due to hold separate meetings on Thursday afternoon to try and reach a breakthrough in the months-long dispute.
"Today is the moment of truth," Figurati told reporters. "I think today we will represent in a conclusive way the situation as it is currently."
Treu said earlier he hoped to be able to submit a proposal to metalworkers by Saturday to end the dispute over contracts.

Leaders from Italy's three main trade union confederations met Prime Minister Romano Prodi earlier for a first round of talks. Treu, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco and Industry Minister Pier Luigi Bersani were also present at that meeting.

Unions representing 1.7 million workers in the metalworking and engineering sector, which accounts for about 40 percent of total manufacturing output in Italy, are locked in dispute with management over pay increases for the 1996-1998 period.
Union leaders told reporters that Federmeccanica was unimpressed with what the government was planning to offer.
Metalworkers' contracts expired in June and unions have recently held two national strikes in support of their claims for wage rises.
